title: Credible Intervals vs Confidence Intervals
interviewAnswer: A Bayesian credible interval is a probability statement about a parameter under the posterior; a frequentist confidence interval is a procedure that covers the fixed parameter at a stated long-run frequency.
keyPoints: Interpretations differ even when numerical intervals look similar.
Frequentist coverage is about repeated procedures.
why: Credible Intervals vs Confidence Intervals appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Interpretations differ even when numerical intervals look similar.
deepDive: A Bayesian credible interval is a probability statement about a parameter under the posterior; a frequentist confidence interval is a procedure that covers the fixed parameter at a stated long-run frequency. Bayesian intervals depend on prior/model. Frequentist coverage is about repeated procedures. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A 95% credible interval can be described as containing 95% posterior probability for the parameter under the model.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Credible Intervals vs Confidence Intervals make?
How would you validate or debug Credible Intervals vs Confidence Intervals in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
